verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）耶和华―我的磐石是应当称颂的！他教导我的手争战，教导我的指头打仗。
verses.en: By David.The Lord, my Protector,[NOTE:1] deserves praise[NOTE:2]—the one who trains my hands for battle[NOTE:3] and my fingers for war,
notes: Psalm 144. The psalmist expresses his confidence in God, asks for a mighty display of divine intervention in an upcoming battle, and anticipates God’s rich blessings on the nation in the aftermath of military victory.
Heb “my rocky summit.” The Lord is compared to a rocky summit where one can find protection from enemies. See Ps 18:2.
Heb “blessed [be] the Lord, my rocky summit.”

verses.zh: 他是我慈爱的主，我的山寨，我的高台，我的救主，我的盾牌，是我所投靠的；他使我的百姓服在我以下。
verses.en: who loves me[NOTE:1] and is my stronghold,my refuge[NOTE:2] and my deliverer,my shield and the one in whom I take shelter,who makes nations submit to me.[NOTE:3]
notes: The one who trains my hands for battle. The psalmist attributes his skill with weapons to divine enablement (see Ps 18:34). Egyptian reliefs picture gods teaching the king how to shoot a bow. See O. Keel, The Symbolism of the Biblical World, 265.
Heb “my loyal love,” which is probably an abbreviated form of “the God of my loyal love” (see Ps 59:10, 17).
Or “my elevated place.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，人算甚么，你竟认识他！世人算甚么，你竟顾念他！
verses.en: O Lord, of what importance is the human race[NOTE:1] that you should notice them?Of what importance is mankind[NOTE:2] that you should be concerned about them?[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the one who subdues nations beneath me.”
Heb “What is mankind?” The singular noun אֱנוֹשׁ (ʾenosh) is used here in a collective sense and refers to the human race. See Ps 8:5.

Heb “and the son of man.” The phrase “son of man” is used here in a collective sense and refers to human beings. For other uses of the phrase in a collective or representative manner, see Num 23:19; Ps 146:3; Isa 51:12.

verses.zh: 人好像一口气；他的年日如同影儿快快过去。
verses.en: People[NOTE:1] are like a vapor,their days like a shadow that disappears.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “take account of him.” The two imperfect verbal forms in v. 4 describe God’s characteristic activity.
Heb “man,” or “mankind.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你使天下垂，亲自降临，摸山，山就冒烟。
verses.en: O Lord, make the sky sink[NOTE:1] and come down.[NOTE:2] Touch the mountains and make them smolder.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his days [are] like a shadow that passes away,” that is, like a late afternoon shadow made by the descending sun that will soon be swallowed up by complete darkness. See Ps 102:11.

The Hebrew verb נָטָה (natah) can carry the sense “to [cause to] bend; to [cause to] bow down.” For example, Gen 49:15 pictures Issachar as a donkey that “bends” its shoulder or back under a burden. Here the Lord causes the sky, pictured as a dome or vault, to sink down as he descends in the storm. See Ps 18:9.
Heb “so you might come down.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose after the preceding imperative. The same type of construction is utilized in v. 6.

verses.zh: 求你发出闪电，使他们四散，射出你的箭，使他们扰乱。
verses.en: Hurl lightning bolts and scatter the enemy.Shoot your arrows and rout them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “so they might smolder.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose after the preceding imperative.

verses.zh: 求你从上伸手救拔我，救我出离大水，救我脱离外邦人的手。
verses.en: Reach down[NOTE:1] from above.Grab me and rescue me from the surging water,[NOTE:2] from the power of foreigners[NOTE:3]
notes: Arrows and lightning bolts are associated in other texts (see Pss 18:14; 77:17-18; Zech 9:14), as well as in ancient Near Eastern art (see R. B. Chisholm, “An Exegetical and Theological study of Psalm 18/2 Samuel 22” [Th.D. diss., Dallas Theological Seminary, 1983], 187).
Heb “stretch out your hands.”
Heb “mighty waters.” The waters of the sea symbolize the psalmist’s powerful foreign enemies, as well as the realm of death they represent (see the next line and Ps 18:16-17).

verses.zh: 他们的口说谎话；他们的右手起假誓。
verses.en: who speak liesand make false promises.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “from the hand of the sons of foreignness.”

verses.zh: 神啊，我要向你唱新歌，用十弦瑟向你歌颂。
verses.en: O God, I will sing a new song to you.Accompanied by a ten-stringed instrument, I will sing praises to you,

verses.zh: 你是那拯救君王的；你是那救仆人大卫脱离害命之刀的。
verses.en: the one who delivers[NOTE:1] kingsand rescued David his servant from a deadly[NOTE:2] sword.
notes: Heb “who [with] their mouth speak falsehood, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood.” The reference to the “right hand” is probably a metonymy for an oath. When making an oath, one would raise the hand as a solemn gesture. See Exod 6:8; Num 14:30; Deut 32:40. The figure thus represents the making of false oaths (false promises).
Heb “grants deliverance to.”

verses.zh: 求你救拔我，救我脱离外邦人的手。他们的口说谎话；他们的右手起假誓。
verses.en: Grab me and rescue me from the power of foreigners[NOTE:1] who speak liesand make false promises.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “harmful.”
Heb “from the hand of the sons of foreignness.”

verses.zh: 我们的儿子从幼年好像树栽子长大；我们的女儿如同殿角石，是按建宫的样式凿成的。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] our sons will be like plants,that quickly grow to full size.[NOTE:2] Our daughters will be like corner pillars,[NOTE:3] carved like those in a palace.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “who [with] their mouth speak falsehood, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood.” See v. 8 where the same expression occurs.

Some consider אֲשֶׁר (ʾasher) problematic, but here it probably indicates the anticipated consequence of the preceding request. (For other examples of אֲשֶׁר indicating purpose/result, see BDB 83 s.v. and HALOT 99 s.v.) If the psalmist—who appears to be a Davidic king preparing to fight a battle (see vv. 10-11)—is victorious, the whole nation will be spared invasion and defeat (see v. 14) and can flourish. Some prefer to emend the form to אַשְׁרֵי (“how blessed [are our sons]”). A suffixed noun sometimes follows אַשְׁרֵי (ʾashre; see 1 Kgs 10:8; Prov 20:7), but the presence of a comparative element (see “like plants”) after the suffixed noun makes the proposed reading too awkward syntactically.

Heb “grown up in their youth.” The translation assumes that “grown up” modifies “plants” (just as “carved” modifies “corner pillars” in the second half of the verse). Another option is to take “grown up” as a predicate in relation to “our sons,” in which case one might translate, “they will be strapping youths.”
The Hebrew noun occurs only here and in Zech 9:15, where it refers to the corners of an altar.

verses.zh: 我们的仓盈满，能出各样的粮食；我们的羊在田间孳生千万。
verses.en: Our storehouses[NOTE:1] will be full,providing all kinds of food.[NOTE:2] Our sheep will multiply by the thousandsand fill[NOTE:3] our pastures.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “carved [in] the pattern of a palace.”
The Hebrew noun occurs only here.
Heb “from kind to kind.” Some prefer to emend the text to מָזוֹן עַל מָזוֹן (mazon ʿal mazon, “food upon food”).
Heb “they are innumerable.”

verses.zh: 我们的牛驮着满驮，没有人闯进来抢夺，也没有人出去争战；我们的街市上也没有哭号的声音。
verses.en: Our cattle will be weighted down with produce.[NOTE:1] No one will break through our walls,no one will be taken captive,and there will be no terrified cries in our city squares.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in outside places.” Here the term refers to pastures and fields (see Job 5:10; Prov 8:26).

Heb “weighted down.” This probably refers (1) to the cattle having the produce from the harvest placed on their backs to be transported to the storehouses (see BDB 687 s.v. סָבַל). Other options are (2) to take this as reference to the cattle being pregnant (see HALOT 741 s.v. סבל pu) or (3) to their being well-fed or fattened (see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 288).

verses.zh: 遇见这光景的百姓便为有福！有耶和华为他们的　神，这百姓便为有福！
verses.en: How blessed are the people who experience these things.[NOTE:1] How blessed are the people whose God is the Lord.
notes: Heb “there [will be] no breach, and there [will be] no going out, and there [will be] no crying out in our broad places.”
